purpose: Cannabidiol is used to help control certain types of severe seizures in people with specific epilepsy conditions, including Dravet syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and tuberous sclerosis complex. It can significantly reduce how often these seizures happen. It is a natural compound derived from the cannabis plant but does not cause a 'high.'
how_it_works: Cannabidiol works in the brain by calming down overactive nerve signals that cause seizures. It interacts with several systems in the brain and nervous system to help keep electrical activity more stable and controlled. Scientists are still learning exactly how it does this, but the result is fewer and less severe seizures for many patients.
common_side_effects: Sleepiness or tiredness, decreased appetite, diarrhea, upset stomach or nausea, irritability or mood changes, trouble sleeping, and infections. Some people also notice their liver enzymes go up, which is why your doctor will monitor your blood work.
warnings: Cannabidiol can cause serious liver problems, especially if you are taking valproate (Depakote) at the same time — tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain. It can make you very drowsy, so be careful driving or operating machinery. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can make seizures worse. Tell your doctor about ALL other medications you take because cannabidiol interacts with many drugs. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 1 year and older, dosing is based on body weight and is usually started low and slowly increased over time. A typical starting dose is about 2.5 mg per kilogram of body weight twice a day. The dose may be increased up to a maximum of 10–20 mg per kilogram per day depending on your condition and how well you tolerate it. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and use the measuring device provided.
